R0042.title: Fake Inventory
R0042.definition: An e-commerce seller deliberately claims to have stock of a product when they do not actually have sufficient inventory.
R0042.description: Fake inventory generally serves a few purposes: first, attracting users with extremely low prices or popular items, then claiming out-of-stock and redirecting users to other products; second, creating fake inventory to attract orders, then fulfilling them through reselling or other means.
R0042.influence: The first type of fake inventory creates a poor shopping experience for users, who may feel deceived; the second type may cause delayed shipments or users paying high prices for low-value goods, negatively impacting user experience.

references.title: How Are Tmall Sellers Penalized for Fake Inventory?

observables: A seller's listed inventory quantity severely mismatches its actual fulfillment capacity, with a large volume of delayed shipments after orders are placed
A seller sets high inventory on low-price SKUs but actually ships substitute high-price SKUs
Multiple products from the same seller show a high proportion of out-of-stock orders where items become unavailable immediately after ordering
A seller's inventory fluctuates sharply and inconsistently with sales volume, such as listing large quantities then rapidly dropping to zero
User complaints concentrate on a seller with similar descriptions of listing items as available while out of stock or inducing purchase switches
